title: NFR-009 Performance: turn latency is recorded per run with no fabricated SLA
risk: Latency numbers on dashboards are estimates or are pre-filled with target values, so a performance regression is invisible and an SLA is claimed that was never measured.
preconditions: Namespace gov-nfr-<case_id>-<worker_id>; NFR verification runs against the offline gateway with mock SoR and channel boundaries.
Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z; failure, outage and crash injections are scripted at the substituted boundary, never faked inside the assertion.
No official SLA exists: NFR-009 states the SLA is locked only after benchmark, and ASM-002 KPI targets are unapproved.

steps.action: Run one complete turn with a known injected workload duration
steps.expected: The run record contains latency_ms at least 850 and the audit row field 16 is populated.

steps.action: Inspect where the latency value comes from
steps.expected: The value is measured between real start and end timestamps using the monotonic clock, not copied from a target or a constant.

steps.action: Compare the displayed dashboard value with the stored run value
steps.expected: They agree; the dashboard does not substitute a target or a rounded placeholder.

steps.action: Attempt to assert an SLA from the measurement
steps.expected: No SLA assertion is possible because no benchmark has been run; the case records the measurement as NOT_RUN for SLA conformance rather than PASS.

assertions: Latency is recorded per run from measured timestamps and the recorded value is at least the injected workload duration.
The value is never a constant, a target or a default: two runs with different injected durations produce different values.
No SLA or percentile target is asserted as a pass bar; the absence of a benchmark is reported explicitly.
Dashboard and stored values agree exactly.
forbidden: Hardcoding a target latency as the measurement.
Recording zero when the timer cannot be read.
Claiming SLA compliance from a single synthetic measurement.
evidence: Run record with latency_ms, plus the audit row field 16.
Measurement source trace showing the timestamp pair used.
cleanup: Delete gov- run rows after export.
automation: Core PEP, rules engine, audit writer, idempotency store and worker lease logic run as real code under test; only ERP/WMS, channel gateways, Redis and the model provider are substituted. Faults are injected at those boundaries and waits are condition-based on persisted state.
prerequisites: The formal latency SLA does not exist (locked only after the NFR-009 benchmark and ASM-002 baseline); this case must not be reported as SLA acceptance.
note: Generated acceptance specification. Plain specification, not an executable test; no application runtime exists, so the status is NOT_RUN.
